newsitem.title: USA: STRONG DOLLAR REFLECTS U.S. ECONOMY-FED'S PHILLIPS.
newsitem.headline: STRONG DOLLAR REFLECTS U.S. ECONOMY-FED'S PHILLIPS.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve governor Susan Phillips said on Thursday that the current dollar strength reflected the good performance of the U.S. economy. She also warned that there may be increased currency volatility ahead of Europe's planned single currency.
"The economic situation is pretty strong here, so the currency is probably reflective of that," Phillips told Reuters in an interview.
Phillips said the run-up to Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) had triggered uncertainty in financial markets, which in turn had caused increased currency volatility.
"I understand this concern by speculators, and a lot of investors internationally, that just see the dollar as more of a safe haven," Phillips said.

"I think as we move towards and around these various trigger points in the Maastricht Treaty (on EMU) we could well get some volatility ... which I think is not necessarily driven by what I would consider the fundamentals," she added.
Phillips said she believed, however, that there were "overbearing forces" which would eventually drive currencies to an economic equilibrium.
She added that recent events in Asian currency markets had contributed to a heightened sense of uncertainty among investors.

"I'd like to think that some of these things are temporary and will settle down, so that the relative values can be consistently reflective of the underlying economic fundamentals," the Fed governor said.
The collapse of the Thai baht has had repercussions in many Asian markets and forced Thailand to seek a loan package backed by the International Monetary Fund.
